```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

# The workbooks behind the screenshots go to a temporary folder. The screenshots are
# made from the same code by data-raw/vignette-screenshots.R with Microsoft Excel and
# are stored in man/figures/; they are shown at half their pixel width, their size in Excel.
fig_dir <- normalizePath("../man/figures", mustWork = FALSE)
out_dir <- Sys.getenv("TSG_VIGNETTE_OUT", file.path(tempdir(), "facade"))
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = out_dir)

shot <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("facade-", name, ".png"))
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(invisible())
  header <- readBin(path, "raw", 24)
  width <- sum(as.integer(header[17:20]) * 256^(3:0))
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf(
    '<div style="overflow-x:auto"><img src="%s" width="%d" alt="Excel sheet: %s" style="max-width:none;height:auto"></div>',
    knitr::image_uri(path), width %/% 2, name
  ))
}
```

```{r setup}
library(tsg)
library(dplyr)
```

`tsg` uses a **style** object (called a *facade*) to control how your tables look when exported: fonts, colours, borders, cell sizes, and more. You can:

- Use a **built-in style** out of the box,
- **Tweak a few settings** with `add_facade()`, or
- **Design your own style** by editing a YAML template.

The same style applies consistently to all output formats (Excel, HTML, PDF, Word).

---

## Using a built-in style

The package ships with thirteen named styles. Pass a name to any writer via the `facade` argument: a style looks the same in Excel, HTML, PDF and Word.

| Style name | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `"default"` | Clean, neutral; used automatically when no style is specified |
| `"yolo"` | Bolder colours and heavier formatting |
| `"apa"` | APA style: horizontal rules only, no fills, Times New Roman |
| `"booktabs"` | Thick top and bottom rules, a thin rule under the header, nothing else |
| `"striped"` | Coloured header band and banded body rows |
| `"gridded"` | Thin lines around every cell and a grey header, as in statistical yearbooks |
| `"minimal"` | No borders or fills, light grey rules between rows; suits web and dashboards |
| `"financial"` | Dark blue header, thin grey grid and a bold last row, as in business reports |
| `"nyt"` | Editorial: bold header over a thick rule, no vertical lines, light banding |
| `"jama"` | Medical-journal: horizontal rules only, bold sans-serif header and first column |
| `"dark"` | Light text on a dark background |
| `"pastel"` | Soft blue header and group titles |
| `"census"` | Official statistics: grey header, bold group titles, small italic notes |

```{r, eval=FALSE}
tbl <- person_record |>
  generate_frequency(sex)

write_xlsx(tbl, path = "booktabs.xlsx", facade = "booktabs")
write_html(tbl, path = "booktabs.html", facade = "booktabs")
write_docx(tbl, path = "booktabs.docx", facade = "booktabs")

# The default style is used when you leave out `facade`
write_xlsx(tbl, path = "default.xlsx")
```

Only `"default"` differs a little between formats (for example, Word uses a smaller font). Every other style is laid over that format's default. Settings that only mean something in a spreadsheet, such as row heights and column widths, are ignored outside Excel.

Here is each style in Excel (a screenshot of the sheet `write_xlsx()` writes) and in HTML (built with `as_gt()`, which returns the styled `gt` table for your own Quarto or R Markdown documents):

```{r, include = FALSE}
gallery_tbl <- person_record |>
  generate_crosstab(marital_status, sex) |>
  add_table_title("Marital status by sex") |>
  add_source_note("Source: person_record")

facades <- c("default", "yolo", "apa", "booktabs", "striped", "gridded", "minimal",
             "financial", "nyt", "jama", "dark", "pastel", "census")

for (f in facades) {
  write_xlsx(gallery_tbl, paste0("facade-", f, ".xlsx"), facade = f)
}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", purl = FALSE}
for (f in facades) {
  cat("\n\n#### `", f, "`\n\n**Excel**\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(shot(f))
  if (requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat("\n\n**HTML**\n\n")
    cat(gt::as_raw_html(as_gt(gallery_tbl, facade = f)))
  }
}
```

---

## Tweaking a few settings with `add_facade()`

`add_facade()` lets you override individual style settings without replacing the whole style. Call it in your pipeline before `write_*()`.

Style settings use a two-part name: **which part of the table** `.` **what to change**. For example:

- `header.fgFill`: fill colour of the column header
- `body.fontSize`: font size of the data cells
- `table.offsetRow`: blank rows above the table (Excel only)

```{r}
person_record |>
  generate_frequency(sex) |>
  add_facade(
    table.offsetRow = 2,
    table.offsetCol = 1
  )
```

### Common tweaks

```{r}
person_record |>
  generate_crosstab(marital_status, sex) |>
  add_facade(
    # Move the table down 2 rows and right 1 column (Excel only)
    table.offsetRow = 2,
    table.offsetCol = 1,
    # Round numbers to 1 decimal place
    table.decimalPrecision = 1,
    # Make the last row (usually Total) bold
    table.lastRowBold = TRUE,
    # Header background colour and white text
    header.fgFill = "#003366",
    header.fontColour = "#FFFFFF",
    header.textDecoration = "bold",
    # Data cell font size
    body.fontSize = 11
  ) |>
  write_xlsx(path = "styled-table.xlsx")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
shot("tweaks")
```

> **Good to know:** A few settings only mean something in a spreadsheet: row heights (`height`), column widths (`width`, `table.widthOffset`), `table.offsetRow`, `table.offsetCol`, `table.gridLines`, `table.tabColour`, `table.locked`, `table.hidden`, `indent` and `wrapText`. HTML, Word and PDF ignore them, so you can attach them once and export to any format without changing anything.

### Borders

Borders take three settings per part: `border` (which sides: `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"`), `borderColour` and `borderStyle`. Border styles use the Excel names in every format; HTML, PDF and Word draw the nearest line:

| `borderStyle` | HTML / PDF | Word |
|---|---|---|
| `"thin"`, `"hair"` | 1px solid | 0.75pt solid |
| `"medium"` | 2px solid | 1.5pt solid |
| `"thick"` | 3px solid | 2.25pt solid |
| `"dashed"`, `"mediumDashed"` | 1px / 2px dashed | 0.75pt / 1.5pt dashed |
| `"dotted"` | 1px dotted | 0.75pt dotted |
| `"double"` | 3px double | 2.25pt double |
| `"dashDot"`, `"dashDotDot"`, `"slantDashDot"` and their `medium` forms | dashed | dashed |

The parts with borders are `body` (every data cell), `header` (every header cell), `spanner` (the upper header rows of a crosstab), `border_header` (the rule under the header) and `border_outer` (the outline around header and body). `body.bandFill` shades every other data row.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
person_record |>
  generate_crosstab(marital_status, sex) |>
  add_facade(
    border_outer.border = c("top", "bottom"),
    border_outer.borderStyle = "medium",
    border_header.border = "bottom",
    border_header.borderStyle = "thin",
    body.bandFill = "#F2F2F2"
  ) |>
  write_html(path = "rules.html")
```

### Applying the same tweaks across formats

Once you attach style overrides with `add_facade()`, those overrides are carried with the table object and applied to whichever format you export to. You only need to style the table once.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
styled_tbl <- person_record |>
  generate_frequency(sex) |>
  add_table_title("Distribution by Sex") |>
  add_source_note("Source: Survey 2024") |>
  add_facade(
    header.fgFill = "#003366",
    header.fontColour = "#FFFFFF",
    header.textDecoration = "bold",
    body.fontSize = 11,
    table.lastRowBold = TRUE
  )

write_xlsx(styled_tbl, path = "table.xlsx")
write_html(styled_tbl, path = "table.html")
write_pdf(styled_tbl, path = "table.pdf")
write_docx(styled_tbl, path = "table.docx")
```

## Making your own style file

For full control, generate a starter YAML file, edit it to your taste, and load it back in.

### Step 1: generate the template

```{r, eval=FALSE}
generate_template("my-style.yaml", template = "facade")
```

### Step 2: edit the file

Open `my-style.yaml` in any text editor. It looks like this:

```yaml
table.fontName: 'Arial'
table.fontSize: 12
table.offsetRow: 0
table.offsetCol: 0
table.decimalPrecision: 2
table.lastRowBold: false
table.width: 14

header.fgFill: ~          # ~ leaves the setting off
header.fontColour: ~
header.textDecoration: ~
header.height: 28

body.fontSize: ~
body.bgFill: ~
body.numFmt: "###0"
body.height: 20

title.fontSize: 13
title.textDecoration: "bold"
title.height: 24

source_note.fontSize: 10
source_note.textDecoration: "italic"
```

Change any value you like. A setting set to `~` is turned off; a setting you delete from the file comes from the default facade.

> **Tip:** `get_tsg_facade()` also accepts `.json` file paths if you prefer JSON over YAML.

### Step 3: use your style

Pass the file's path as the `facade` of any writer:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
tbl <- person_record |>
  generate_frequency(sex)

write_xlsx(tbl, path = "custom-styled.xlsx", facade = "my-style.yaml")
write_docx(tbl, path = "custom-styled.docx", facade = "my-style.yaml")
```

---

## Programmatic style overrides

If you need to build style settings dynamically (for example, in a loop or from a config), keep them in a named list and pass it to `add_facade()` with `do.call()`, or pass the list as the `facade` of a writer.

```{r}
overrides <- list(
  table.offsetRow = 3,
  header.fgFill = "#2E4057",
  header.fontColour = "#FFFFFF",
  body.fontSize = 11
)

do.call(
  add_facade,
  c(list(data = person_record |> generate_frequency(sex)), overrides)
)
```

---

## Style property reference

The table below lists every setting supported by each section of the table.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
props <- c(
  "fontName", "fontSize", "fontColour",
  "bgFill", "fgFill",
  "halign", "valign",
  "textDecoration", "wrapText", "indent",
  "border", "borderColour", "borderStyle",
  "numFmt", "height", "width"
)

sections <- c(
  "table", "title", "subtitle", "header", "spanner",
  "body", "col_first", "col_last", "row_group", "sub_group",
  "source_note", "footnotes"
)

has_prop <- function(section, prop) {
  if (prop == "width")  return(section %in% c("table", "col_first", "col_last", "row_group"))
  if (prop == "numFmt") return(section %in% c("body", "col_first", "col_last"))
  if (prop == "height") return(section != "table")
  TRUE
}

ref <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sections, function(s) {
  data.frame(
    Section = s,
    Properties = paste(
      Filter(function(p) has_prop(s, p), props),
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

knitr::kable(ref, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Table-level settings (full list)

| Setting | What it does | Excel | HTML | Word |
|---------|-------------|:-----:|:----:|:----:|
| `table.fontName` | Default font family | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.fontSize` | Default font size | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.fontColour` | Default font colour | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.bgFill` | Table background colour | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.decimalPrecision` | Decimal places for numbers | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.decimalCols` | Which columns get decimal formatting | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.lastRowBold` | Make the last row bold | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `table.offsetRow` | Blank rows above the table | ✓ | | |
| `table.offsetCol` | Blank columns to the left | ✓ | | |
| `table.gridLines` | Show worksheet grid lines | ✓ | | |
| `table.tabColour` | Excel worksheet tab colour | ✓ | | |
| `table.locked` | Lock the worksheet | ✓ | | |
| `table.hidden` | Hide the worksheet | ✓ | | |
| `table.width` | Column width | ✓ | | |
| `table.widthOffset` | Extra width added to auto-sized columns | ✓ | | |

### Colour values

`fgFill` is the fill colour of a cell. `bgFill` is the background of a fill pattern in Excel, so it shows only behind a pattern; HTML and Word use it when `fgFill` is not set. All `fontColour`, `bgFill`, and `fgFill` settings accept:

- Hex colour codes: `"#003366"`
- Named R colours: `"navy"`
- `~` (in YAML) or `NULL` (in R) to use the inherited default

### Section names

| Section | What it styles |
|---------|----------------|
| `table` | Global table settings |
| `title` | Title row above the table |
| `subtitle` | Subtitle row |
| `header` | Column header row(s) |
| `spanner` | Grouped header rows in cross-tabulations |
| `body` | Data rows |
| `col_first` | First (category) column |
| `col_last` | Last column |
| `row_group` | Group header rows |
| `sub_group` | Sub-group rows |
| `source_note` | Source note row below the table |
| `footnotes` | Footnote rows |
| `border_header` | Border under the header |
| `border_outer` | Outer border around the table |
| `border_bottom` | Bottom border row height |
